name: Nick Klein
event: UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Nolan
summary: A Pura Vida BJJ middleweight (6-3, 0-2 UFC) and Contender Series winner who starts like a house on fire with kicks, takedowns and back takes, then has been stopped in R2 of both UFC fights. Hasn't fought since August 2025.

how_they_fight.Striking: Long (196 cm reach) and kicks a lot early; landed a spinning backfist/elbow that wobbled Mansur Abdul-Malik in R1 (Cageside Press, MMA Mania). Striking is mostly a lead-in to wrestling; about 3.1 significant strikes a minute.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Primary weapon: 3.6 takedowns per 15 minutes and 1.1 sub attempts per 15. Three of his six wins are submissions (two in R1, including a 37-second finish on DWCS, one in R3). Took Andrey Pulyaev down three times in R1, forced his back and threatened a neck crank before losing position (Cageside Press). Struggles to finish shots against a real wrestler: 1 of 9 vs Abdul-Malik.
how_they_fight.Defense: Stopped in all three losses, all by strikes: Dorjan Dokaj (R3), Abdul-Malik (punches and knees from the back, R2) and Pulyaev (body kick and punches, R2, per Cageside Press). Gives up position when scrambles go wrong.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Front-loaded. Finishes: R1 4 (two KOs inside 30 seconds, two subs), R3 1 (sub); one decision. Losses: R3 KO (regional), then R2 TKOs in both UFC fights (3:24, 1:31). Cageside Press described him as visibly fatigued in R2 against Abdul-Malik after a failed takedown-heavy R1; against Pulyaev he won R1 clearly and was stopped 91 seconds into R2. Fair to call him a fader against durable opposition.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Commits hard to the takedown, even when he had Abdul-Malik hurt on the feet (he shot instead of following up, per Cageside Press). Needs to pace himself better.

patterns: Explosive R1: kicks, takedowns, back takes
R2 stoppage losses in both UFC fights after big first rounds
Finishes come early (four in R1) or by late submission
concerns: 14-month layoff; 0-2 in the UFC and likely fighting for his job
Opponent Joseph Kropschot (9-3, five straight wins, DWCS) per BoxingNews
keys_to_beat: Defend the R1 takedown flurry and stay off your back
Body work and pressure early in R2 when his tank dips
Punish failed shots; he's been finished off scrambles

news.text: Booked against Contender Series winner Joseph Kropschot (9-3) for Oct. 31, Kropschot's UFC debut (BoxingNews).
Lost to Andrey Pulyaev by R2 TKO (1:31) after winning R1 with takedowns.
